reason: All four questions (including the optional weather one) are answered from real 2023-2024 Citi Bike data (79.41M raw trips, 79,371,599 kept after cleaning; 0.049% removed, each rule reported). I independently re-queried /app/parquet and reproduced the 24 monthly counts, the clean total, and the weekday/weekend peak hours by rider type; all match output/tables. Findings are backed by tables with bootstrap CIs and by figures. Remaining gaps are limitations to state in the report (unverified 2023 zip provenance, peak-month ambiguity, one-point weather proxy), not reasons for more experiments. I could not view figures myself (host copy was denied); the write-report job reported inspecting them, so the writer should confirm legibility.

findings.statement: Monthly volume is strongly seasonal: lowest in winter (Jan/Feb), highest in a broad summer-autumn plateau. Peak/trough ratio is about 2.3 (2023) and 2.7 (2024) on monthly totals, and 2.2 (CI 2.07-2.42) and 2.7 (CI 2.49-3.14) per day. The exact peak month is not well pinned down (Aug 2023, Oct 2024 by totals; bootstrap agreement 55-88%). 2024 exceeds 2023 in every month (about 1.26x overall).

Weekdays show two commute peaks, at 08:00 and 17:00, in both years (100% of bootstrap resamples agree). The 08:00 peak is about 1.5x the 11-14h midday mean and the 17:00 peak about 2.0x (2023: 1.46 and 1.97; 2024: 1.54 and 2.04). Excluding federal holidays shifts ratios by only 0.03-0.04. Weekends have a single broad midday/afternoon peak, centred at 15:00 (a plateau, 54-98% bootstrap agreement depending on year/season). Weekend days are less busy than weekdays on average, and Sunday is the lowest day of the week (about 0.85-0.88 of the weekly mean).
evidence: my re-query of 2024 clean trips: member weekday top hours 17,18,8; weekend 15,14,13

findings.statement: Members and casual riders differ. Casual riders take a larger share of trips on weekends (35.4% vs 23.3% for members in 2023, similar in 2024; CIs do not overlap). On weekdays members have both an 08:00 and a 17:00 peak, while casual riders have a weak or absent morning peak and a smaller evening peak. Weekday profile distance is moderate (Jensen-Shannon about 0.12), weekend profiles are nearly identical (about 0.06). Casual riding is much more seasonal (casual peak/trough about 4.4 in 2023 and 5.4 in 2024, vs about 2.1 and 2.5 for members). Casual trips are also longer (median about 13-14 min vs about 8.4-8.6 for members).
evidence: my re-query: casual weekday 2024 top hours 17,18,16 (08:00 not in top 3)

findings.statement: Daily trip counts are positively associated with temperature (Spearman rho 0.73, block-bootstrap CI 0.62-0.78; casual 0.81, member 0.66) and negatively with precipitation (rho -0.29, CI -0.38 to -0.19). In an adjusted log model, relative to dry days trips are about 9% lower on 0-2.5 mm days, 23% lower on 2.5-10 mm, and 42% lower above 10 mm. The temperature effect is nonlinear (about +38% per +10C from 10 to 20C, about +11% from 20 to 30C). Within-month the temperature coefficient stays about +3.7%/C, so the association is not only shared seasonality, but season (daylight, school, tourism) cannot be fully separated. Association only, not causal.

Data cleaning removed only 38,596 of 79,410,195 raw trips (0.049%; 27,230 in 2023, 11,366 in 2024). Dominant rule is duration > 24h (37,576). The 643 negative-duration rows are all on the two fall-back DST dates (artifact of repeated 01:00 hour), not bad data. Findings are insensitive to cleaning: dropping or keeping the sub-60s trips changes 182 rows.

Which month is the single peak, and which weekday is busiest, are not robust: the peak month changes between years and between total vs per-day measures, and the weekday ordering is not consistent between years. Reports should describe a summer-autumn plateau rather than name one peak month.

open_questions: The 2023 data came from the yearly zip, not the monthly files (monthly 2023 URLs return 404), so equivalence with the original monthly files is unverified. Row counts and date ranges look plausible.
R5 (duration > 24h) removed 26,640 trips in 2023 vs 10,936 in 2024 and this was not investigated. It is below 0.08% of trips, so it does not change any finding.
How much of the 2024-over-2023 growth reflects the electric share rising from 50.2% to 66.1%, fleet or station expansion, or demand, cannot be separated with these data.
Weather uses one Central Park grid point for the whole city; borough-level or hourly weather was not tested.
Casual vs member is the system's label, whose definition may have changed over time; it is not verified here and cannot be checked within these two years.

active_hypotheses.statement: Citi Bike volume is strongly seasonal, with a winter trough (Jan/Feb) and a broad summer-autumn plateau, with the same shape in 2023 and 2024.
supporting_evidence: Peak/trough 2.3 (2023) and 2.7 (2024); 2024/2023 ratio above 1 in all months
Independent re-query reproduced the 24 monthly counts
contradicting_evidence: Peak month differs between years (Aug vs Oct) and bootstrap agreement is only 55-88%, so a single peak month is not supportable

active_hypotheses.statement: Weekday use is commute-driven (peaks at 08:00 and 17:00), while weekend use is leisure-shaped (single broad peak around 15:00).
supporting_evidence: Peak hours 8 and 17 with 100% bootstrap agreement in both years
Holiday exclusion changes ratios by only 0.03-0.04
contradicting_evidence: Commute purpose is inferred from timing only; no trip-purpose data. Weekend peak hour is a plateau, with 2024 agreement of 54-73%.

active_hypotheses.statement: Members behave more like commuters and casual riders more like leisure/tourist riders: casual share is higher on weekends, casual weekday mornings lack a peak, casual trips are longer and much more seasonal.
supporting_evidence: Weekend share 35.4% vs 23.3% (2023) with non-overlapping CIs
Median duration about 13-14 vs about 8.5 min
contradicting_evidence: Weekend hourly shapes nearly identical (JS about 0.06); weekday difference is moderate (about 0.12), so the two groups overlap substantially
Intent behind the labels is not observed

active_hypotheses.statement: Day-to-day trip volume rises with temperature and falls with rain, over and above seasonal and calendar structure.
supporting_evidence: Full-model R2 0.80 vs 0.62 for month plus calendar
contradicting_evidence: Residual autocorrelation (Durbin-Watson 1.15) means intervals may be narrow
Single-point weather proxy and unmeasured seasonal confounders (daylight, school calendar, tourism)

active_hypotheses.statement: Results are an artifact of data quality or cleaning.
contradicting_evidence: Negative durations are explained by DST

inferred_mechanisms: Commute-driven weekday demand, mostly from members, produces the 08:00 and 17:00 peaks; the evening peak is larger than the morning one.

Discretionary and tourist-type riding, concentrated among casual riders, is the main driver of weekend afternoon use and of strong seasonality, with weather acting as a gating factor on that discretionary demand.
Weather (cold, rain) suppresses trips on top of seasonal pattern; the effect is roughly proportional (log scale) and saturates at high temperatures.
Year-over-year growth (about 1.26x) is system-wide across all months and coincides with a rise in e-bike share, but this study cannot attribute cause.
unresolved_ambiguity: Exact peak month and busiest weekday are not stable across years.
How much of the temperature association is true weather response vs seasonal co-movement.
Provenance of the 2023 yearly zip vs the original monthly files.
Whether the rider-type definition changed within the study period.
mental_model.current_rationale: Citi Bike usage in 2023-2024 follows a clear and robust pattern: strong seasonality with a winter trough and summer-autumn plateau, weekday commute peaks at 08:00 and 17:00, a weekend afternoon peak around 15:00, casual riders who are more weekend- and season-oriented than members, and daily volume that tracks temperature and rain. These were verified by an independent re-query and are stable under the cleaning and holiday/DST sensitivity checks. Findings are descriptive associations from one city and two years; the peak month and weekday ordering should be reported as uncertain.
